contract_inferred: No 00-contract.md. Inferred from the page: an app screen (a weekly-ops dashboard, 'Northline weekly ops', with stat figures, filters, an Urgent table, pending items, an empty state, contact actions and a 35-row 'Campaign tracker' table of repos, forks and pull requests). The page labels itself 'Skill fixture, before' and 'Basic HTML … No design system', so it is a test fixture; it is judged here as the layout that ships. Visitor mode Operate. English only (html lang en), US formats (dollars, 'Oct 13, 2026', '9:14am', 'EST'). No right-to-left language.
overall_reason: Plain static HTML reads fully without script, weighs almost nothing and lets every cell wrap, but the six-column campaign tracker has no phone treatment and widens the whole page to 773px at 375.

score.reason: T-NO-SCRIPT, T-WEIGHT-FOR-JOB, T-LOCALE-FORMAT and T-EXTREME-COUNTS pass, but T-WIDTHS fails on the campaign tracker at 375 (ROB-010, with the sweep's ROB-003 overflow Floor).

findings.title: The layout holds between and beyond the captured widths
findings.evidence: At 375 the six-column table is 749px wide and sits directly in the page, not in a scroll box, so the document is 773px wide (parity.document_widths; the sweep's overflow Floor names the table). The Fork and PR columns start past the screen (long_unbroken_strings: 'VibeRooster/cool-claude-skills' at x 489, inside_viewport false). tiles/375-02.png to tiles/375-05.png show the PR column squeezed to about 55px with notes such as 'not opened yet (branch add-before-after-example); after pinned' set two words per line. This matches draft ROB-209 (a phone table with two or more columns off-screen).
findings.before: A wide data table with no phone layout and no scroll container; the whole page scrolls sideways.
findings.after: Wrap the table in a container with overflow-x: auto and a sticky first column, or below 640px render each row as a stacked card (repo as the title, skill, fork and PR as labelled lines).
findings.why: A phone user loses the Fork and PR columns off the right edge, and the sideways page scroll also moves the Urgent table and every heading above it.

strengths: All 4,323 characters are in the HTML and stay visible with scripts off, with an observer that never fires and with reduced motion.
The page makes 2 requests with an LCP of 756 ms and uses the system face, so nothing late can move the text.
Table cells wrap long repo names and notes at their hyphens instead of clipping them (text_risk shows no nowrap or clipped rows; tiles/1440-01.png).
The filtered list has a written empty state ('No matching threads in this filter.'), and counts and money use one style ('128 Open threads', '$18,400', 'Oct 13, 2026').
not_investigated: T-STRESS: no hostile content was injected; long names were judged from layout evidence.
A right-to-left render and translated strings were not captured.
The page load was not throttled and layout shift was not measured as a number (capture predates the CLS record).
The fail runs of 'Send follow-up', 'Remove' and the other actions were skipped because the slow runs made no request.

The 'Review required 1/5' chip (#vr-hitl-chip) floats over the Urgent table at 375 and over the Empty section at 1440 (tiles/375-00.png); it reads as review tooling added to the fixture, not the page's own layout.
The compact '$42.6k' pipeline figure beside full figures such as '$18,400' is a single-surface style mix at most; not raised.
Widths between the captures, landscape, zoom at 200%, back navigation and deep links.
